wcs.crval_note: target astrometric position seen from Earth at the first visit
wcs.pixel_convention: PNG pixels: origin at top-left image corner, x right, y down, pixel centre at i+0.5

frame.combine: per detector: nanmean of background-subtracted exposures; visit = nanmean over detectors
frame.f32: float32 little-endian, n×n, row 0 = north (top), col 0 = east (left); MJy/sr, background-subtracted; NaN = no data
frame.not_masked: SOURCE (label), DICHROIC, GHOST*, CROSSTALK, STREAK, BLOOM, SNOWBALL, HALO, OVERFLOW/NONLINEAR (would remove bright-star cores)

stretch.formula: v = asinh((x - vmin)/soft) / asinh((vmax - vmin)/soft), clipped to [0,1]

longterm.note: Straight-line space motion (no Galactic potential / no orbit); ±20,000 yr, 100 yr step

notes: Earth barycentric position is used for the observer; SPHEREx orbits ~650 km above Earth (parallax effect < 1e-4 arcsec, ignored).
Directions are astrometric (no annual aberration), matching Gaia-tied SPHEREx WCS.
rv_kms=null is computed as 0 km/s in 3D.
photometry_note: aperture r=2.5 px (15.4″), background annulus 4.5–8 px, in the original detector pixels; mJy, not aperture-corrected — compare one detector over time, or one visit across wavelength. Saturated cores: ring 2.5–4.5 px mean surface brightness (MJy/sr), relative only
